facts.statement: Dinichthys was an extinct genus of large marine arthrodire placoderm measuring approximately 3 meters in length.
facts.quote: Dinichthys (from , 'terrible' and 'fish') is an extinct monospecific genus of large marine arthrodire placoderm from the Late Devonian (Famennian stage) measuring around 3 m long.

facts.statement: Fossils of Dinichthys were recovered from the Ohio Shale Formation near the Olentangy River in Delaware County, Ohio.
facts.quote: Fossils were recovered from the Ohio Shale Formation along the Olentangy River in Delaware County, Ohio.

facts.statement: Dinichthys was originally described in 1868 by John Newberry based on an incomplete skull roof and mandibles.
facts.quote: Dinichthys was originally described in 1868 by John Newberry on the basis of an incomplete skull roof and mandibles (holotype AMNH 81).

facts.statement: A 2010 phylogenetic study found that Dinichthys and Dunkleosteus belong to two separate clades.
facts.quote: However, in the 2010 Carr & Hlavin phylogenetic study, Dunkleosteus and Dinichthys were found to belong to two separate clades.

facts.statement: The family Dinichthyidae is now considered monospecific, containing only the genus Dinichthys and its type species D. herzeri.
facts.quote: Dinichthyidae, in turn, is left a monospecific family and dismissed as a family grouping, and the genus Dinichthys is now considered a monotypic genus, containing only the type species, D. herzeri.

facts.statement: Dinichthys was a genus of placoderm arthrodire fish that lived during the Late Devonian (Famennian) in Ohio and Tennessee, USA.
facts.quote: Dinichthys (gr. "pez terrible") es un género de peces placodermos artrodiros que vivieron a finales del período Devónico (Famenniano) de Ohio y Tennessee, Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: Dinichthys was comparable in size, shape, and ecological role to the well-known Dunkleosteus.
facts.quote: Era comparable en tamaño, forma y rol ecológico al mejor conocido Dunkleosteus.

facts.statement: Many illustrations supposedly representing Dinichthys are actually images of Dunkleosteus.
facts.quote: Como resultado, muchas ilustraciones que supuestamente representan a Dinichthys son realmente imágenes de Dunkleosteus

facts.statement: Dinichthys lived from the Givetian to the Famennian stages, between 387.95 and 358.86 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Givetian to Famennian (387.95 to 358.86 million years ago)
